extraction_text: Sage Shaunaka requests Sauti to narrate the story of Sage Astika in detail.

relationships: Shaunaka is the listener, Sauti is the narrator

extraction_text: Sauti agrees to narrate the story of Sage Astika as he heard it from his father.

relationships: Sauti is the son of a storyteller

extraction_text: In ancient times, Prajapati had two daughters named Kadru and Vinata.

relationships: Kadru and Vinata are daughters of Prajapati

extraction_text: Kadru and Vinata both became wives of Sage Kashyapa.

relationships: Kadru and Vinata are co-wives of Kashyapa

extraction_text: Kashyapa grants each wife a boon. Kadru wishes for a thousand snake sons with equal splendor. Vinata wishes for two sons who are stronger, more brilliant, and braver than Kadru's sons.

relationships: Kashyapa is the husband granting boons
Kadru and Vinata are competing wives

extraction_text: Kashyapa grants Vinata's boon partially, saying she will get one and a half sons.
After conception, Kashyapa instructs his wives to protect their pregnancies and goes to the forest for penance.
Kadru lays a thousand eggs, and Vinata lays two eggs. The eggs are placed in moist pots and incubated for five hundred years.

relationships: Kadru and Vinata are both expecting children

extraction_text: After five hundred years, Kadru's thousand snake sons hatch from the eggs, but Vinata's two sons do not appear.

relationships: Kadru's sons are born, Vinata's are delayed

extraction_text: Impatient, Vinata breaks one egg and finds a son with only the upper half of his body developed.

relationships: Vinata is the mother, Aruna is the son

extraction_text: The half-formed son curses Vinata to become a slave of Kadru for five hundred years, and says her other son will free her.

relationships: Vinata will be enslaved to Kadru

extraction_text: A son curses Vinata for wanting to break the remaining egg prematurely.

attributes.reason: To prevent Vinata from causing the unborn child to be born deformed
supernatural_elements: Prophecy about the child's required gestation period of 500 years

extraction_text: Aruṇa flies into the sky and becomes the red dawn.

attributes.result: Manifests as the red dawn at daybreak

extraction_text: Garuda is born from the egg after the full gestation period.

attributes.description: Garuda, the great eagle and slayer of serpents, is born on time

extraction_text: Garuda immediately leaves Vinata after birth and flies high into the sky to seek his own food.

attributes.reason: To obtain the food that the Creator (Brahma) has arranged for him
